text:
Evan K: Heads-up — during this morning's PTQ bring-up for the reranker we saw NDCG@10 go up ~1.5% but MRR drop ~3%. seems contradictory, filing here to collect quick hypotheses.

Priya S: Can you paste the eval config and a quick summary of the evaluation pool?

Evan K: Sure — quick config: 
```
model: reranker-v2-2026
quant: PTQ-8bit-gpu
eval_sets: product-search:holdoutA, faq:holdoutB
metric: ndcg@10, mrr@10, recall@100
cand_gen: bm25+onnx_ann
```
Pool size ~ 10k queries, ~ 50k candidates per query pre-filter. NDCG@10 +1.5%, MRR@10 -3.0%, recall@100 -0.6%.

Cheng L: Interesting — a tiny recall drop with NDCG up and MRR down suggests top-1 moved around a lot but rank distribution improved below top. Do you have per-query delta histogram?

Evan K: Uploaded a quick breakdown: median rank change for relevant doc = +1 (worse) but 75th percentile improved by 2 ranks. So many queries got slightly worse top hit, but lots of mid-ranked answers moved up.

Priya S: That would explain ndcg improving (graded positions) while MRR (which cares about first hit) falls. Any chance label granularity differs between product-search and faq? MRR will be more sensitive on sparse binary labels.

Evan K: Good call — product-search uses graded labels (0/1/2) while faq is binary. When I isolate product-search NDCG up 2.3% and MRR change ~-0.5%. On faq NDCG flat, MRR -6%.

Cheng L: Sounds like quantization noise is reshuffling score ordering near the top for the binary set. Could be small logit scaling differences. Try re-scaling logits or calibrating temperature post-PTQ, or run a config where logits remain float (quantize weights only).

Evan K: Agreed. I ran a quick ablation: weights-quantized + activations float => MRR -0.8% (much smaller). weights+acts quant => -3%. So activation quant looks responsible.

Priya S: Also double-check candidate generation recall curves. If bm25+onnx_ann lost some head candidates for faq (lower recall for exact-match queries), reranker can't fix that.

Evan K: Candidate recall at 100 dropped 0.6% overall, but for faq subset it's 1.2% (bad). So two contributors: recall drop + activation quant ranking jitter.

QA Bot: regression-report.pdf uploaded: s3://redwood-eval/rerank/1827654321/regression-report.pdf :white_check_mark:

Cheng L: Another idea — MRR is sensitive to tokenization/normalization differences if reranker uses token-level pooling that depends on punctuations. Any change in input preprocessing in the quantized path?

Evan K: Nope preprocessing identical. But we did enable int8 kernel fused ops in the runtime for quant path; might change attention scaling subtly. I'll spin a run with original runtime but PTQ weights to isolate kernel differences.

Priya S: Also let's surface per-query examples where top-1 changed. Could be helpful to see error modes (typo queries, exact-match reliance, long queries).

Evan K: Will collect top-100 queries where MRR delta <-0.2 and attach examples. Plan: 1) run weights-only PTQ on original runtime, 2) calibrate activation scaling, 3) per-query diffs + spot-check labels. Assigning myself to run these.

Cheng L: Thanks. If you want I can help instrument a small rerank ablation that toggles activation quantization and logging logits diffs for top-10.

Evan K: Appreciate it — please do. Will post results here once I have the per-query artifacts. :eyes:
